style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: A three-part modular assembly on a garage concrete floor: a cast-aluminum walk-behind mower deck with its top cowling and blank grey badge plate lifted and propped open on a small brass hinge, an empty nameplate recess exposed, and a heavy-duty orange extension cord with a large yellow GFCI plug disconnected and lying beside it. Single hard directional key light from the left rakes across the concrete, throwing long shadows. Palette: graphite, rust, bone white. Matte painted steel and weathered concrete texture, hard clean edges, generous negative space on the right, extreme asymmetric three-quarter view. No text, no garbled lettering, no watermarks, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, logos, embossed wording, moulded letters, numbers
rationale: The recall gate and the split between badge and importer are a single rule-level shift, so a restrained modular assembly of recognizable mower hardware states it precisely without text. It keeps the frame in the home garage world while avoiding the previous lettering rejection.
subject: a walk-behind mower deck with its blank brand badge plate lifted away and a severed GFCI-equipped power cord on a garage concrete floor
core_thesis: What decides whether a defective outdoor machine gets repaired, refunded or thrown away is the importer behind the label, not the brand on it.
core_conflict: Brand badge versus importer liability: the licensed name on the machine remains, but the responsible US entity may not stock parts or answer a recall.
composition: extreme asymmetric three-quarter view with open negative space on the right
alt_text: A walk-behind mower deck with its badge plate lifted open and a coiled power cord on a concrete garage floor.
caption: A blank badge plate and a power cord: the two parts that decide who answers for a failed machine.
title: The Importer, Not The Brand, Answers Recalls

review.depicts: A metal walk-behind mower deck lying on its side with a hinged, blank white cover plate lifted open beside it, and a coiled orange extension cord with a yellow GFCI plug resting on a stained concrete floor, with empty floor space at right.
review.reason: The frame shows the article's own object and mechanism — a walk-behind mower deck with its blank badge plate removed, plus a severed cord matching the recall and 'license/badge' framing — so the headline reads as consistent with the image.
